name: Crescent Lunge
hero_alt: Crescent Lunge, seen from the side
meta_description: Front knee not reaching 90°, back knee bending, torso tipping forward, arms short of overhead? Three things usually hold back Crescent Lunge, and how to fix each.
og_description: Three things usually hold back Crescent Lunge, and a daily exercise that fixes each one.
lede: Front knee over the ankle at a right angle, back heel lifted with the leg straight, torso tall, arms reaching up. Here’s the rubric Posewise measures it against, and what to train when you miss.
rubric_intro: Posewise checks six things from the side. Here’s what good looks like.

rubric.name: Front knee
rubric.good: Bent to a right angle, over the ankle

rubric.name: Back heel
rubric.good: Lifted, over the ball of your foot

rubric.name: Arms
rubric.good: Straight up, in line with your ears

fixes.outcome: your front knee will reach a 90° bend.
fixes.why: The shape is there, the depth isn’t. That usually points to leg strength, not technique.
fixes.cue: Bend your front knee toward 90°, right over your ankle.

fixes.action: Lengthen your hip flexors and quads
fixes.outcome: your back leg will straighten and your torso will stay tall.
fixes.why: Tight hip flexors and quads on the back leg bend the knee and tip the pelvis, so the chest leans forward.
fixes.cue: Press back through your back heel and lift your chest.

fixes.outcome: your arms will reach straight up, in line with your ears.
fixes.why: When shoulder range runs out overhead, the arms angle forward and the shoulders creep toward the ears.
fixes.cue: Reach your arms up in line with your ears, through your fingertips.

cues: And one cue: stay up on the ball of your back foot. If the heel drops, you’re in Warrior I; if it shoots very high, step that foot further back.

faq.q: What’s the difference between Crescent Lunge and Warrior I?
faq.a: In Crescent Lunge your back heel is lifted and your back toes point forward. In Warrior I the back heel is down, with the foot turned out about 45°.

faq.q: Should my back knee be straight in Crescent Lunge?
faq.a: Yes, long and active, pressing back through your heel. If that’s too much, lower the back knee to the mat for a low lunge.

faq.q: How do I balance better in Crescent Lunge?
faq.a: Keep your feet hip-width apart, not on one line, and firm both legs. Fix your gaze on a point that isn’t moving.

faq.q: How can I check my Crescent Lunge form at home?
faq.a: Film yourself from the side. Or use Posewise, an iPhone app that measures your Crescent Lunge with the camera, speaks corrections as you hold it, and builds a six-minute daily plan for what it finds.

llms_summary: the three things that usually hold back Crescent Lunge (leg strength for a 90° front knee, tight hip flexors and quads bending the back leg and tipping the torso, shoulder mobility for arms overhead), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
